114:     #[doc = include_str!("../docs/routing/route.md")]
115:     pub fn route<T>(mut self, path: &str, service: T) -> Self
116:     where
117:         T: Service<Request<B>, Response = Response, Error = Infallible> + Clone + Send + 'static,
118:         T::Future: Send + 'static,
119:     {
120:         if path.is_empty() {
121:             panic!("Invalid route: empty path");
122:         }
123: 
124:         let service = match try_downcast::<Router<B>, _>(service) {
125:             Ok(_) => {
126:                 panic!("Invalid route: `Router::route` cannot be used with `Router`s. Use `Router::nest` instead")
127:             }
128:             Err(svc) => svc,
129:         };
130: 
131:         let id = RouteId::next();
132: 
133:         let service = match try_downcast::<MethodRouter<B, Infallible>, _>(service) {
134:             Ok(method_router) => {
135:                 if let Some((route_id, Endpoint::MethodRouter(prev_method_router))) = self
136:                     .node
137:                     .path_to_route_id
138:                     .get(path)
139:                     .and_then(|route_id| self.routes.get(route_id).map(|svc| (*route_id, svc)))
140:                 {
141:                     // if we're adding a new `MethodRouter` to a route that already has one just
142:                     // merge them. This makes `.route("/", get(_)).route("/", post(_))` work
143:                     let service =
144:                         Endpoint::MethodRouter(prev_method_router.clone().merge(method_router));
145:                     self.routes.insert(route_id, service);
146:                     return self;
147:                 } else {
148:                     Endpoint::MethodRouter(method_router)
149:                 }
150:             }
151:             Err(service) => Endpoint::Route(Route::new(service)),
152:         };
153: 
154:         if let Err(err) = self.node.insert(path, id) {
155:             self.panic_on_matchit_error(err);
156:         }

158:         self.routes.insert(id, service);

163:     #[doc = include_str!("../docs/routing/nest.md")]
164:     pub fn nest<T>(mut self, path: &str, svc: T) -> Self
165:     where
166:         T: Service<Request<B>, Response = Response, Error = Infallible> + Clone + Send + 'static,
167:         T::Future: Send + 'static,
168:     {
169:         if path.is_empty() {
170:             panic!("Invalid route: empty path");
171:         }
172: 
173:         if path.contains('*') {
174:             panic!("Invalid route: nested routes cannot contain wildcards (*)");
175:         }
176: 
177:         let prefix = path;
178: 
179:         if path == "/" {
180:             self.nested_at_root = true;
181:         }
182: 
183:         match try_downcast::<Router<B>, _>(svc) {
184:             // if the user is nesting a `Router` we can implement nesting
185:             // by simplying copying all the routes and adding the prefix in
186:             // front
187:             Ok(router) => {
188:                 let Router {
189:                     mut routes,
190:                     node,
191:                     fallback,
192:                     // nesting a router that has something nested at root
193:                     // doesn't mean something is nested at root in _this_ router
194:                     // thus we don't need to propagate that
195:                     nested_at_root: _,
196:                 } = router;
197: 
198:                 if let Fallback::Custom(_) = fallback {
199:                     panic!("Cannot nest `Router`s that has a fallback");
200:                 }
201: 
202:                 for (id, nested_path) in node.route_id_to_path {
203:                     let route = routes.remove(&id).unwrap();
204:                     let full_path = if &*nested_path == "/" {
205:                         path.to_owned()
206:                     } else {
207:                         format!("{}{}", path, nested_path)
208:                     };
209:                     self = match route {
210:                         Endpoint::MethodRouter(method_router) => self.route(
211:                             &full_path,
212:                             method_router.layer(layer_fn(|s| StripPrefix::new(s, prefix))),
213:                         ),
214:                         Endpoint::Route(route) => {
215:                             self.route(&full_path, StripPrefix::new(route, prefix))
216:                         }
217:                     };
218:                 }
219: 
220:                 debug_assert!(routes.is_empty());
221:             }
222:             // otherwise we add a wildcard route to the service
223:             Err(svc) => {
224:                 let path = if path == "/" {
225:                     format!("/*{}", NEST_TAIL_PARAM)
226:                 } else {
227:                     format!("{}/*{}", path, NEST_TAIL_PARAM)
228:                 };
229: 
230:                 self = self.route(&path, strip_prefix::StripPrefix::new(svc, prefix));
231:             }
232:         }
233: 
234:         self
235:     }

472:     #[inline]
473:     fn call(&mut self, mut req: Request<B>) -> Self::Future {
474:         if req.extensions().get::<OriginalUri>().is_none() {
475:             let original_uri = OriginalUri(req.uri().clone());
476:             req.extensions_mut().insert(original_uri);
477:         }
478: 
479:         let path = req.uri().path().to_owned();
480: 
481:         match self.node.at(&path) {
482:             Ok(match_) => self.call_route(match_, req),
483:             Err(err) => {
484:                 if err.tsr() {
485:                     let redirect_to = if let Some(without_tsr) = path.strip_suffix('/') {
486:                         with_path(req.uri(), without_tsr)
487:                     } else {
488:                         with_path(req.uri(), &format!("{}/", path))
489:                     };
490:                     let res = Response::builder()
491:                         .status(StatusCode::MOVED_PERMANENTLY)
492:                         .header(http::header::LOCATION, redirect_to.to_string())
493:                         .body(crate::body::empty())
494:                         .unwrap();
495:                     RouterFuture::from_response(res)
496:                 } else {
497:                     match &self.fallback {
498:                         Fallback::Default(inner) => {
499:                             RouterFuture::from_future(inner.clone().call(req))
500:                         }
501:                         Fallback::Custom(inner) => {
502:                             RouterFuture::from_future(inner.clone().call(req))
503:                         }
504:                     }
505:                 }
506:             }
507:         }
508:     }

511: fn with_path(uri: &Uri, new_path: &str) -> Uri {
512:     let path_and_query = if let Some(path_and_query) = uri.path_and_query() {
513:         let new_path = if new_path.starts_with('/') {
514:             Cow::Borrowed(new_path)
515:         } else {
516:             Cow::Owned(format!("/{}", new_path))
517:         };
518: 
519:         if let Some(query) = path_and_query.query() {
520:             Some(
521:                 format!("{}?{}", new_path, query)
522:                     .parse::<http::uri::PathAndQuery>()
523:                     .unwrap(),
524:             )
525:         } else {
526:             Some(new_path.parse().unwrap())
527:         }
528:     } else {
529:         None
530:     };
531: 
532:     let mut parts = http::uri::Parts::default();
533:     parts.scheme = uri.scheme().cloned();
534:     parts.authority = uri.authority().cloned();
535:     parts.path_and_query = path_and_query;
536: 
537:     Uri::from_parts(parts).unwrap()
538: }

540: // we store the potential error here such that users can handle invalid path
541: // params using `Result<Path<T>, _>`. That wouldn't be possible if we
542: // returned an error immediately when decoding the param
543: pub(crate) struct UrlParams(
544:     pub(crate) Result<Vec<(ByteStr, PercentDecodedByteStr)>, InvalidUtf8InPathParam>,
545: );

547: fn insert_url_params<B>(req: &mut Request<B>, params: Vec<(String, String)>) {
548:     let params = params
549:         .into_iter()
550:         .map(|(k, v)| {
551:             if let Some(decoded) = PercentDecodedByteStr::new(v) {
552:                 Ok((ByteStr::new(k), decoded))
553:             } else {
554:                 Err(InvalidUtf8InPathParam {
555:                     key: ByteStr::new(k),
556:                 })
557:             }
558:         })
559:         .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>();
560: 
561:     if let Some(current) = req.extensions_mut().get_mut::<Option<UrlParams>>() {
562:         match params {
563:             Ok(params) => {
564:                 let mut current = current.take().unwrap();
565:                 if let Ok(current) = &mut current.0 {
566:                     current.extend(params);
567:                 }
568:                 req.extensions_mut().insert(Some(current));
569:             }
570:             Err(err) => {
571:                 req.extensions_mut().insert(Some(UrlParams(Err(err))));
572:             }
573:         }
574:     } else {
575:         req.extensions_mut().insert(Some(UrlParams(params)));
576:     }
577: }

While working on routes for an app, I wanted to add admin routes under /admin/.... I've got my routes in two modules, app and admin. I'm nesting them from the parent like so:
// main.rs
Router::new()
    .nest("/", app::routes())
    .nest("/admin", admin::routes())
and the app routes are:
// app.rs
Router::new()
    .route("/", get(foo::list))
    .route("/foo", get(foo::list).post(foo::create))
and the admin routes are:
// admin.rs
Router::new()
   .route("/", get(bar::list))
   .route("/bar", get(bar::list).post(bar::create))
I'd expect the above to produce the following route table:
GET / -> foo::list
GET /foo -> foo::list
POST /foo -> foo::create
GET /admin -> bar::list
GET /admin/bar -> bar::list

GET / -> 404
GET //foo -> foo::list
POST //foo -> foo::create
(the rest is as expected)

I'm able to fix this by dropping the leading / from the nested app (foo) routes. I tried nesting them at "", but that won't compile. part.text:
Fixed the issue in `axum/src/routing/mod.rs`:

- **Double-slash bug**: when nesting a `Router` at `/`, nested routes like `/foo` produced `//foo` (and the nested `/` route swallowed `GET /` incorrectly). Now, when `path == "/"`, the nested path is used as-is, so `nest("/", app_routes())` yields `/`, `/foo`, etc. as expected (axum/src/routing/mod.rs:205).
- **`nest("")`**: instead of panicking on the empty path, it now means the same as `nest("/")` (axum/src/routing/mod.rs:170).

Verification: all 125 lib tests pass — including `nesting_router_at_empty_path`, `nesting_router_at_root`, `nesting_handler_at_root`, and the nest-root panic-message tests. The 3 remaining doctest failures are pre-existing and unrelated (missing `headers`/`TypedHeader` feature in doc examples).
